subject: Customer Readout: Short model rollback on Dedicated pool — investigation summary and verification plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@greenbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Briefing: Dedicated pool rollback observed this morning — quick sync?

Hi Emily,

Wanted to flag a short incident we observed this morning affecting one of GreenBank's dedicated inference pools. At ~08:02 PT a model rollback (automated fallback) triggered for a small percentage of your requests, which caused a transient latency increase and 1xx token truncations for some long-running requests. The issue lasted about 7 minutes and there was no data exfiltration.

We're assembling a concise readout and would like to schedule a 30-minute customer briefing today or tomorrow to walk through:
- What triggered the rollback
- Timeline and affected scope
- Immediate mitigations we applied
- Verification steps and a proposed fix schedule

Proposed times: today 11:00–11:30 PT or tomorrow 09:30–10:00 PT. If those don't work, please suggest a slot. We'll share a short RCA doc and a verification checklist ahead of the call.

Apologies for the disruption — we know low-latency inference is critical for your workflows.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident-evidence-stub.txt (log fragments, 10KB)

From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@greenbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-07T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Briefing: Dedicated pool rollback observed this morning — quick sync?

Thanks for the heads up, Karthik.

We saw a handful of failed responses in our logs around 08:02 — some of our downstream processes retried and we logged higher end-to-end latency. No customer-facing errors reported, but we'd like the timeline and root cause. Tomorrow 09:30–10:00 PT works for us. Can you confirm the specific customer IDs/instances impacted so our compliance team can reconcile?

Also please include any Playbook steps we should run on our side to speed verification.

-Emily
Emily Ross
Head of SRE, GreenBank Financial

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-09T13:00:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident readout and verification plan — Dedicated pool rollback (summary attached)

Emily / GreenBank SRE team,

Thanks again for taking the meeting this morning. As promised, attached is a concise two-page readout plus a verification checklist for your team. Below is a short executive summary, timeline, root cause, and the actions we've committed to.

Executive summary
- Incident window: 2026-10-07 08:02:14–08:09:46 PT. (7m32s)
- Impact: ~0.6% of requests to your dedicated pool experienced a fallback to an earlier model revision; of those, ~12% observed token truncation behavior requiring client retries. No evidence of data leakage or unauthorized access.
- User impact: internal retries and elevated latency for a small subset of background jobs; no customer-facing outages reported.

Incident timeline (high level)
- 08:02:05 PT: autoscaling job performed a rolling update to a model variant for a maintenance window (scheduled but with a mismatched rollout policy).
- 08:02:14 PT: routing controller detected a kernel mismatch and triggered automated rollback to a previous model variant for a fraction of hosts to preserve SLOs.
- 08:04:30 PT: monitoring fired elevated latency alerts; redundancy and cache-prefetch safeguards limited broader impact.
- 08:09:46 PT: rollout completed and all hosts returned to the expected model revision; monitoring cleared.

Root cause
- A configuration drift in the Dedicated pool's rollout policy caused a subset of hosts to receive a model variant that was not fully validated for your long-sequence workload. The runtime's automated protection performed a targeted rollback, but the rollback path did not fully rehydrate KV-caches for a small number of in-flight sessions which caused token truncation for those requests.

Immediate mitigations applied
- We paused the scheduled rollout and reverted the per-cluster policy settings.
- Forced KV-cache rehydrate for affected hosts and invalidated stale prefixes.
- Deployed an alert rule to catch partial rollback-induced cache inconsistencies.

Committed next steps (timeline)
- 2026-10-09 (completed): Delivery of this readout and the verification checklist.
- 2026-10-12: Engine patch to ensure cache rehydration occurs atomically with rollback.
- 2026-10-19: Additional pre-rollout validation tests for long-sequence models in Dedicated pools.
- 2026-10-26: Post-deployment verification window with GreenBank SRE (joint runbook exercise).

Customer verification steps (attached checklist)
- Run the attached verification script against a non-prod replica (instructions included).
- Confirm there are no token truncation traces in your 08:00–09:00 PT logs for 2026-10-07.
- Share a quick confirmation email once checks are complete; we'll follow up to close the ticket.

Attachments included
- 20261009-karthik-kv-divergence-rca.pdf (2 pages, executive readout)
- greenbank-verification-checklist-20261009.xlsx (checklist and runbook steps)

Links
- Post-incident doc: https://redwood-drive.internal/docs/GreenBank-PostIncident-Readout-20261009
- Internal ticket: JIRA INF-8721

Apologies again for the disruption. We consider this high priority and will share test results and the engine patch notes as they are available. If you'd like a follow-up call next week for the verification exercise, suggest times and we'll reserve dedicated engineering.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
